title: Tedizolid Targets AQP9-JAK/STAT Axis to Suppress Metastatic Progression in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma: Mechanism and Therapeutic Implications.
authors: Qu, Kexin; Zhang, Tianya; Wang, Rui; Bi, Yingwei; Jin, Jiacheng; Liu, Yuxin; Yi, Bolin; Zhu, Liang; Wang, Jianbo
one_liner_zh: 该文研究AQP9蛋白在肾癌转移中的作用及药物Tedizolid的靶向抑制，虽含分子对接但核心是蛋白-小分子互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA体系，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Metastasis is a primary driver of poor outcomes in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), yet the role of Aquaporin-9 (AQP9) in this process remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the function, clinical significance, and therapeutic potential of AQP9 in ccRCC. AQP9 expression was analyzed using TCGA data and validated in human tissues and cell lines via Western blot. Functional assays assessed malignant behaviors, while bioinformatics and rescue experiments explored the involvement of the JAK/STAT pathway and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Virtual screening, molecular docking, and cellular thermal shift assays (CETSAs) were employed to identify Tedizolid as a potential AQP9 inhibitor, followed by functional validation in vitro and in a xenograft model. AQP9 was significantly upregulated in ccRCC and associated with poor prognosis. The knockdown of AQP9 suppressed proliferation, migration, invasion, and EMT, whereas its overexpression promoted these effects by activating the JAK/STAT pathway. Tedizolid bound directly to AQP9, inhibited cell viability, reversed AQP9-induced malignant phenotypes, and suppressed JAK/STAT signaling both in vitro and in vivo. In conclusion, AQP9 promotes ccRCC metastasis through the JAK/STAT-EMT axis and represents a potential prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target. Tedizolid, identified as a novel AQP9 inhibitor, offers a promising repurposed strategy for ccRCC treatment.
abstract_zh: 转移是透明细胞肾细胞癌（ccRCC）预后不良的主要驱动因素，然而水通道蛋白-9（AQP9）在此过程中的作用仍不清楚。本研究旨在探讨AQP9在ccRCC中的功能、临床意义及治疗潜力。利用TCGA数据分析AQP9表达，并通过Western blot在人组织和细胞系中进行验证。功能实验评估恶性行为，而生物信息学和拯救实验探讨了JAK/STAT通路及上皮-间质转化（EMT）的参与。通过虚拟筛选、分子对接和细胞热位移分析（CETSAs）鉴定Tedizolid为潜在的AQP9抑制剂，随后在体外和异种移植模型中进行功能验证。AQP9在ccRCC中显著上调，并与不良预后相关。敲低AQP9抑制了增殖、迁移、侵袭和EMT，而其过表达通过激活JAK/STAT通路促进了这些效应。Tedizolid直接结合AQP9，抑制细胞活力，逆转AQP9诱导的恶性表型，并在体外和体内抑制JAK/STAT信号传导。总之，AQP9通过JAK/STAT-EMT轴促进ccRCC转移，并代表一种潜在的预后生物标志物和治疗靶点。Tedizolid作为一种新型AQP9抑制剂，为ccRCC治疗提供了一种有前景的药物再利用策略。
